evidence.label: authentication_model
evidence.detail: no authentication appears in the source we fetched, but this server's network endpoint is a hosted remote, whose authentication can be enforced in front of its code — and no credential header is declared. An undeclared header is not an absent one, so `03` §4's "no authentication" band is not established.

evidence.label: transport_security
evidence.detail: declared endpoint(s) are HTTPS: https://mcp.certscore.ai/mcp; scored 80, not 100: `03` §4 reserves 100 for HTTPS *with HSTS*, and an HSTS header can only be seen by connecting, which `04` §9 does not do. This is an unverifiable band, not an observed absence.

evidence.label: secret_handling
evidence.detail: detect-secrets matched 25 credential-shaped string(s), every one from a keyword or entropy heuristic (Base64 High Entropy String, Hex High Entropy String, Secret Keyword). Those flag placeholders, variable names and content hashes as readily as credentials, so they do not establish the committed credential `03` §4's 0 asserts, and this sub-check is not scored; Secret Keyword at README.md:245; Secret Keyword at dist/certscore-mcp.mjs:17911; Secret Keyword at dist/certscore-mcp.mjs:18027; Hex High Entropy String at dist/certscore-mcp.mjs:20880; Hex High Entropy String at dist/certscore-mcp.mjs:21132; Hex High Entropy String at dist/certscore-mcp.mjs:21132; Hex High Entropy String at dist/certscore-mcp.mjs:21206; Hex High Entropy String at dist/certscore-mcp.mjs:21208; Hex High Entropy String at dist/certscore-mcp.mjs:21214; Hex High Entropy String at dist/certscore-mcp.mjs:21226; …and 15 more matches

evidence.label: authorization_granularity
evidence.detail: no tool registration was recognised anywhere in the source. An MCP server registers tools by definition, so this is a gap in our detection rather than a server with none, and `03` §4's threshold cannot be applied to it.

evidence.label: recency
evidence.detail: last commit 0 day(s) before 2026-11-25

evidence.label: issue_responsiveness
evidence.detail: every issue read was filed by the project itself (2 by its maintainers or bots), so none is someone outside waiting for an answer, and `03` §5's question — will anyone read an issue I file? — has nothing to measure.

evidence.label: release_cadence
evidence.detail: released 22 day(s) ago (by releases), inside `03` §5's 30-day window

evidence.label: bus_factor
evidence.detail: 3 authors with >= 5 commits in 12 months

evidence.label: repository_signals
evidence.detail: `03` §5 scores this by quartile WITHIN the server's category, which needs a distribution across every scanned server and so cannot be computed while scanning one. It is a post-pass over the crawl and that pass does not exist yet.

dependency_health.reason: no lockfile in the published package (npm does not publish a package's package-lock.json; npm-shrinkwrap.json is the lockfile a published package can carry); dependency versions are unresolved, so no vulnerability can be attributed

evidence.label: license
evidence.detail: LICENSE present with no SPDX-License-Identifier tag; text not matched against any license this build can identify (`04` §7's classifier is not wired; see module docstring)

evidence.label: readme_quality
evidence.detail: README.md: installation instructions (+25), configuration documented (+25), exposed tools or resources enumerated (+30), states what the server does in the first 200 words (+20)

evidence.label: declared_scopes
evidence.detail: specific scope or access documentation is present, but `03` §7's 100 and 60 bands both compare it against scopes INFERRED from static analysis, which is not built yet. Scoring 100 on an empty inference would be a vacuous truth — 'all ∅ inferred scopes are documented'.

evidence.label: changelog
evidence.detail: no CHANGELOG in the fetched source. `03` §7's partial credit for tagged releases carrying release notes is not applied here — that needs the forge API, which this check does not call

evidence.label: security_contact
evidence.detail: no SECURITY.md and no disclosure contact in the README, so a finder has no route to report a vulnerability privately
